# Bring-up dependency inventory

Reviewed 24 November 2026. The rewrite targets Fedora 45 AArch64 on `uke`, with the boot image in `boot_a` and Linux on `userdata`. A tester reports that the existing `uke-fedora` port works on their tablet, including builds newer than R1. The exact newer build and device configuration are unconfirmed.

| Stage | Inputs and tools | What the dependency means for bring-up |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kernel compilation | Linux source, matching Senemos configuration and patches, Clang/LLVM, Kbuild tools and device-tree tooling | Deferred for first boot. In the older fork, the native spec takes its sources as RPM inputs and the boot-source staging script builds its archive from files inside Senemos. Neither shows a direct sibling checkout requirement for compilation. The current Senemos release recipe also references a checksum-pinned parent COPR SRPM. A standalone build of the current source has yet to be demonstrated here. [Current Senemos recipe change](https://github.com/MCC45TR/senemos-uke-kernel-mainline/commit/38c2f657506822a73a5bc6e7626e08d6c16ecaec) |
| Kernel packages | Matching ARM64 kernel, modules, DTBs, and boot payload for one exact release | Upstream supports signed package-based image builds. The older spec declares `uke-firmware` for the modules and `uke-nfc-ir`, `uke-boot-integration`, and `uke-kernel-update` for the boot package. The singleboot profile adds `uke-installation-profile`. Check the dependencies of the exact RPMs we select before deciding which userspace pieces the rewrite needs. [Upstream package build guide](https://github.com/MCC45TR/uke-fedora-builder/blob/main/docs/PUBLIC-BUILD.md) |
| Boot image | Kernel payload, compatible initramfs and `userdata` root selector, Android boot header and AVB metadata | Upstream's documented singleboot image uses `boot_b` and expects matching slot-B firmware. The old fork has a distinct `boot_a` recipe. Validate the target slot and the root selector separately before adopting any boot artifact. [Upstream install layout](https://github.com/MCC45TR/uke-fedora-builder/blob/main/docs/PUBLIC-BUILD.md#output-and-manual-installation) · [Fork slot-A recipe](https://github.com/linuxgamer/uke-fedora-builder/blob/6acd2db2a4c1677c45e7046e228bf416d46bf35e/build-fedora44-boot-a.sh) |
| Fedora root filesystem | Fedora AArch64 packages via DNF, the exact kernel module tree, and the device firmware or userspace required for the chosen boot path | The old rootfs builder reads proprietary inputs through the hardware-support repo's verifier and installs several hardware RPMs. That is a dependency of the old image pipeline. Determine the minimum by starting with a console root and an available input method. [Fork rootfs recipe](https://github.com/linuxgamer/uke-fedora-builder/blob/366247338e60f57954f39a95767b57f3e8a8d59a/build-rootfs.sh) |
| Filesystem image | An ext4 filesystem labeled `UKE_LINUX` as required by the Senemos initramfs, filesystem checks, SELinux labeling, and Android sparse encoding | Ext4 is the first candidate because the old slot-A pipeline already uses it. Preserve file ownership and security metadata and verify the sparse image against the raw image before considering a tablet test. [Fork filesystem finalizer](https://github.com/linuxgamer/uke-fedora-builder/blob/366247338e60f57954f39a95767b57f3e8a8d59a/src/image/finalize-rootfs.sh) |

## Prebuilt candidates

- **Historical slot-A reference.** `uke-fedora` R1 shipped a Fedora 44 image pair. Its pinned builder targets `boot_a` and `userdata` with Senemos `7.2.11-34`. The cached `7.2.11-34.fc44.aarch64` RPM set has five members. On Windows, we verified the boot RPM's `linux.img`, embedded kernel, and module-list hashes against its manifest. We matched all 1,157 module paths and individual hashes to the modules RPM. That boot RPM marks `userdata` unsupported. The pinned slot-A recipe changes the initramfs root selection and rebuilds the kernel payload, so use R1 as a reference for that adaptation. The published archive was not downloaded for this review. [R1 release](https://github.com/linuxgamer/uke-fedora/releases/tag/r1) · [R1 image build](https://github.com/linuxgamer/uke-fedora-builder/blob/6acd2db2a4c1677c45e7046e228bf416d46bf35e/build-fedora44-images.sh)
- **Fedora 45 package availability.** MCC45TR's stable and testing Fedora 45 AArch64 COPR indexes contained zero packages when checked. The unstable Fedora 45 index returned HTTP 404. These repositories yielded no Fedora 45 Senemos set. [Upstream package build guide](https://github.com/MCC45TR/uke-fedora-builder/blob/main/docs/PUBLIC-BUILD.md)
- **Rawhide packaging reference.** COPR lists three `7.3.5-47.fc46.aarch64` RPMs from the same source RPM. The merged `core` RPM provides the previous `boot`, `modules`, and `dtbs` capabilities. Its repository file list shows `userdata.img`, `linux.img`, a boot manifest, `modules.sha256`, 821 module paths, and the `uke` DTB. The `core` RPM requires `uke-firmware`, `uke-control`, boot integration and kernel-update capabilities. Those requirements will inform the Fedora 45 dependency check. [Senemos source commit](https://github.com/MCC45TR/senemos-uke-kernel-mainline/commit/38c2f657506822a73a5bc6e7626e08d6c16ecaec)
- **Rawhide verification status.** The metapackage and complete `core` RPM matched the repository SHA-256. Their RSA/SHA-256 header signatures and signed payload digests verified against MCC45TR's published COPR fingerprint. The core's Android boot v4 `userdata.img`, its embedded kernel, and `modules.sha256` matched the package manifest. All 821 module paths matched the RPM contents. The `singleboot` RPM, Fedora 45 dependency resolution, and `boot_a` compatibility remain unverified. The acquired artifacts and metadata are in the ignored `build/cache/senemos-upstream/` directory. [Published signing fingerprint](https://github.com/MCC45TR/uke-linux/releases/tag/fedora-rawhide-uke-senemos-021126-r4)

## Local firmware evidence

- The local OS3.0.304.0.WOZMIXM stock boot image matched the old slot-A recipe's SHA-256 and size of 100,663,296 bytes.
- All 219 files in the old firmware bundle matched the two reference manifests and the separately pinned touch reference by size and SHA-256. This checks the local inputs against the old recipe. The first-boot subset remains to be identified for the chosen kernel.
- Shared inputs include touch panel profiles, SSC files, Bluetooth firmware and ADSP, WPSS, WLAN and GPU firmware. A measured touch reference came from a running Android tablet. Keep device identifiers and calibration out of the generic ZIP. Keep captured device-specific inputs local.

## Fedora 45 console experiment

The official Fedora 45 x86_64 WSL2 distribution loaded Fedora 45 AArch64 metadata and attempted a DNF dry run of the signed `7.3.5-47.fc46` core and metapackage. The base Fedora repositories could not satisfy the Uke-specific requirements, including firmware, boot integration, installation profile support, `uke-control`, and the kernel updater. No packages were installed. The Windows host did not need AArch64 emulation for the resolver test.

A second dry run resolved the Fedora 45 AArch64 console package list (`fedora-release`, systemd, udev, Bash, coreutils, util-linux, kmod, shadow-utils, PAM, e2fsprogs and the targeted SELinux policy). DNF planned 104 packages with weak dependencies off. The transaction stopped before installation.

| Dependency | Role in first boot |
| --- | --- |
| Senemos kernel, DTB and modules | Keep the verified boot payload and module tree on exactly the same release. The inspected `7.3.5-47` initramfs is embedded in the kernel and contains the UFS and USB drivers, the Uke root guard, and a conditional F2FS growth service. The root guard recognizes the `userdata` partition selector. Slot A remains unverified. |
| Fedora console root | Provide systemd, udev, a login console and the matching module tree. Plan one input path for bring-up, with a USB keyboard as the initial candidate. The kernel image also contains early USB serial diagnostics. |
| `uke-firmware` and boot integration | The inspected initramfs contains no firmware files. Map firmware requests and device setup on the real root by feature. Touch, wireless, Bluetooth, DSP audio and graphics can be investigated independently of the initial console target. Retain the early boot guard and its filesystem checks. |
| Installation-profile and update dependencies | The initramfs runs the early root mount checks itself. Account for the separate installation profile when adding persistent installation state, root growth on the installed system, or kernel updates. The offline console image can be assembled from explicit boot and root inputs. Keep package dependencies intact for any DNF installation or COPR delivery. |
| `uke-control`, speaker runtime, NFC/IR and O82 color packages | Review these when adding their respective hardware and release features, including update health and rollback. The first console target leaves those features out. |

Keep the first experiment on `userdata`. The inspected initramfs also contains an optional `super` seed path gated by `senemos.super=seed4-v1`. That layout is outside this port's bring-up scope.

The prebuilt staging command verifies the pinned RPM, the unchanged boot image, and every installed module against the package manifest. It stages the boot image separately from the Fedora console package transaction. See the [build command](README.md).

The verified upstream `userdata` boot reference and the OEM slot-A template are both 100,663,296-byte Android boot v4 images with no outer ramdisk. The upstream image has no AVB footer. Both `uke-fedora` recipes use the OEM template's AVB properties and rollback index (1788220800 on the reviewed stock image). The local `uke-fedora` checkout at `af121d34c8167dba8c6df09d2bc64aaec0d1dfa9` pins Senemos `7.3.1-106` and uses a native `userdata` payload with the `uke-elfnote-v2` root selector. R1 uses `7.2.11-34` and a separate initramfs and kernel rebuild for slot A.

The rewrite wraps the prebuilt `7.3.5-47` kernel with the reviewed stock template. Host checks verify the AVB hash footer, the `userdata` selector, OEM properties, and the original kernel and initramfs bytes. The builder rejects the upstream boot reference as a stock template. The current slot-A image has booted on Xiaomi Pad 7. See the [build inputs](INPUTS.md) and [hardware status](../BRINGUP.md#preview-status).
